projection.note: canvas_x = (lon*x_factor - origin[0])*scale + canvas_origin[0] ; canvas_y = (-lat - origin[1])*scale + canvas_origin[1]. canvas_origin defaults to [2, 2] when absent, which is what a main projection uses, so it is written only by an inset that needs a different one.
projection.cell_note: Those are CONTINUOUS canvas coordinates. The cell containing a point is floor(x), floor(y) — the rasteriser fills cell i from [i, i+1). Rounding picks the nearest cell CENTRE and lands one cell over for anything past the halfway line; harmless on a large region, decisive on a small child.

index_legend.0: outside the country (sea, neighbour, coastline ink)

base.index_note: one byte per LOGICAL cell, canvas-sized, NOT export_scale. Hit-test against this, not against pixel colour.
base.subject_rect_note: x,y,w,h as fractions of the canvas. Scale the two layers together so this rect fills the intended width; the backdrop bleeds off the screen edges.

carves_note: A first-plane area cut by a published boundary (see region_map.py). It is an ordinary region in regions[] and the index; this block only records where its edge came from and what it was cut from.
